candidates.title: Linear-Time Context Compression with State-Space Encoding
candidates.abstract: Transformer-based large language models (LLMs) impose substantial computation and memory costs as context sizes increase, motivating methods that compress a context into a shorter representation before inference. Existing soft-prompt compression methods typically use the same Transformer backbone as used in the target model, where producing the compressed representation leads to significant latency overheads. This restricts them to the offline setting where context is compressed once and then reused across many queries. We propose the Boa Compressor, a plug-and-play online context compressor built on a Mamba state-space model (SSM) that encodes arbitrary-length context in a single linear-time pass, producing a representation on which we condition a frozen target LLM. The SSM is trained by distillation, matching the next-token logit distribution from the LLM ingesting the full context (as teacher) to the same LLM ingesting the compressed representation (as the student). At equal compression ratios, Boa matches or surpasses the performance of existing state-of-the-art offline compression baselines, while being an order of magnitude faster than Transformer-based implementations, thereby reducing end-to-end latency rather than adding compression time overhead. We demonstrate that Boa also scales well to longer contexts and to compression ratios as aggressive as 16x. By enabling effective compression that is cheap enough to run on every query at inference time, Boa becomes a practical and general tool for efficient long-context inference.
candidates.reason: Transformer系soft-prompt compressorの計算負荷を避け、Mamba SSMが任意長contextを線形時間でencodingし、凍結したtarget LLMへ短い表現として渡すBoa Compressor。full-context teacherとcompressed-context studentの次token logitsを蒸留で一致させる。既存Transformer compressor比約1桁高速で同等以上の圧縮後品質、最大16倍の圧縮率を評価し、online毎query圧縮でend-to-end遅延を削減すると報告。LLM推論時のprompt圧縮としてaccept。

candidates.title: Compiling Autoregressive LLM Control into Policy-Exact Parallel Inference for Hierarchical RAG
candidates.abstract: Large language models increasingly act as controllers in structured decision pipelines, yet their decisions are still executed by autoregressive text decoding. Hierarchical RAG is one such setting: at each frontier of a document tree, an LLM commits to $b$ of $k$ sections under an input-dependent action grammar, executed as either failure-prone free-form JSON or reliable but strictly serial grammar-constrained generation. We show that this serialization is unnecessary for bounded-horizon control: the reachable future forms a shallow action-prefix tree, which we compile --- one root prefill plus one tree-causal probe evaluate every prefix-conditioned action distribution with serial decoding's tokens, positions, and causal ancestry. A prefix-state lemma makes compiled control policy-exact in exact arithmetic: the same policy with a two-forward critical path and zero output tokens. One further probe pass certifies the exact order-marginalized MAP set. Across four document-disjoint splits and two scales on the primary MetaX device, compiled control matches the serial policy on $84$--$89\%$ of questions --- every instrumented divergence a floating-point near-tie --- and cuts control latency by $35$--$47\%$ versus token-wise serial decoding and $6$--$7\%$ versus an idealized chunked engine; an H800 repetition preserves the ordering.
candidates.reason: 階層RAGでb-of-k選択を逐次JSON/grammar decodeする代わりに、有限深度のaction-prefix treeをコンパイルし、root prefillとtree-causal probeで全action-prefix条件付き分布を並列評価する。exact arithmetic下で元の逐次policyと一致する構造を証明し、MetaX実機の4 split/2 scaleで制御latencyを逐次decode比35〜47%、理想chunk engine比6〜7%削減。浮動小数点near-tieで実際の選択一致率は84〜89%と報告。LLM制御出力の推論並列化としてaccept。

candidates.title: SPECMEM: Accelerating Agentic Tool Calling via Live Memory Management
candidates.abstract: Tool-calling agents are mostly optimized for accuracy; in deployment, however, their growing cost is latency: every tool call is decoded autoregressively. Speculative decoding accelerates this without changing the output, and retrieved past calls make strong drafts under real use, where each user's behavior tends to repeat. Yet existing systems keep no cross-session memory, or build the draft store once and never update it. We propose SpecMem, a tool-call memory kept alive and managed throughout deployment: verified calls are written back online into bounded per-user stores with LRU eviction, and a side-effect gate defers irreversible calls until verification confirms. On multi-session, multi-user query streams served by three open-weight models, a frozen store steadily loses acceptance while SpecMem holds it: a 27% gap in mean accepted tokens (+11% to +34% across benchmarks, tracking how much novel work arrives after the store is built) and up to 1.74x wall-clock speedup. Ablations attribute the gain almost entirely to keeping the store live; local per-user scoping adds no acceptance but closes a measured cross-user leakage channel, and gating on declared side effects, rather than on retrieval confidence, is what eliminates irreversible mistakes.
candidates.reason: agentic tool callの自己回帰生成を投機的decodeで加速するため、過去に検証済みのtool callをuser別LRU上限付きstoreへonline書き戻しし、draftを再利用するSpecMem。副作用のあるtool callはtarget検証完了まで実行を遅延させる。3つのopen-weight modelとmulti-session/user query streamで、固定store比平均accepted tokenが27%高く、wall-clock速度最大1.74倍と報告。再利用storeの更新と安全な検証を含むLLM agent servingの直接最適化としてaccept。

candidates.title: Balanced State Subspaces with Spectral Rank Allocation for Mamba-2 State Compression
candidates.abstract: Mamba-2 compresses all context into a fixed-size recurrent state that dominates decoding memory and bandwidth. Existing compressors quantize state values or prune coordinates with per-channel scores. Trained states are nearly rank-one and bias-like, aligned with the mean write; but the output's energy spans an order of magnitude more directions. Per-channel scores see only the diagonal of the write--read operator, so they cannot select the subspace that governs the input--output map, which is a rotation of the coordinates. We therefore propose \method{}, which keeps that subspace by applying balanced truncation exactly via Mamba-2's scalar-identity transition. Layers differ just as sharply: most are bias-dominated, while the few that carry long-range associations are the flattest and need most of their state. We therefore introduce \spar{}, which redistributes a fixed total rank budget across layers according to the Hankel spectrum. On Mamba-2 checkpoints from 130M to 2.7B, \method{}+\spar{} halves the state at an average cost of $0.3$ WikiText-2 perplexity points, against $1.6$ for GHOST, while retaining $97\%$ of the dense model's five-digit in-context recall. At a quarter of the state, giving every layer the same rank keeps $5\%$ of that recall and \spar{} $77\%$, for a $7\%$ perplexity cost.
candidates.reason: Mamba-2 recurrent stateの大きなenergy方向とoutputが読む情報方向が一致しない問題に対し、write/readのcontrollability・observability Gramianを用いたbalanced truncationで状態空間を回転・切り詰める。HARPはHankel spectrumからlayer別rankを配分しretrieval-sensitive layerを保護。130M〜2.7B modelでstate次元半減時のWikiText-2 perplexity悪化平均0.3点（GHOST 1.6点）、較正1 forward passと報告。推論時のSSM state容量・帯域を直接削減するためaccept。

candidates.title: ThinkJev: One Thought, Every Budget for Calibrated Typed Decisions
candidates.abstract: Many uses of language models end in a typed decision: a choice among a closed set of options, whose probabilities code can act on. Reading those probabilities from one forward pass is fast but often wrong on decisions that take several steps, such as arithmetic, counting, and date comparison. Letting the model think first fixes most of these errors, but costs seconds per decision instead of milliseconds. To pay for thinking only where it helps, ThinkJev builds a fast and a slow system from one open hybrid-thinking model that can answer directly or after a thought. System 1 reads the model's probabilities for the option letters when it answers directly; System 2 reads the same letters after the model has thought on the same cached prompt, so escalating repeats no work and both systems give probabilities over the same options. Because the letters can be read after any number of thought tokens, one sampled thought also gives the answer under every thinking budget. Without training, ThinkJev lets System 1 answer alone only where a statistical test on labeled dev data guarantees that its accepted answers stay under a target error rate. At a 5% target, Qwen3.5-27B answers 24.5% of 8359 test decisions this way with a realized error of 3.9% (Qwen3.5-4B and 9B: 6.5% and 0.0%). For the rest, stopping each thought as soon as its answer is confident reaches 81.6% accuracy, against 82.7% for always thinking, with 72% of the thought tokens. Choosing when to think from System 1's confidence alone saves less, because the decisions System 1 is least sure of are often not the ones thinking fixes. On the public items of JevBench, an independent benchmark of typed-decision services, Qwen3.5-27B thinks on 29.4% and is not distinguishable in accuracy from the two thinking APIs listed (exploratory). Code and data generators are available at https://github.com/ding-xiaolu/ThinkJev.
candidates.reason: closed-setのtyped decisionに対し同一hybrid-thinking LLMから高速な直接probability読み取り（System 1）と、同じcached promptで思考後にprobabilityを読むSystem 2を構成。System 1の選択を統計的error-rate gateで制限し、残りは思考中に確信度を満たす時点で停止する。Qwen3.5-27Bで5% error target時24.5%のdecisionをSystem 1のみで処理し、残りを適応停止するとalways-thinkingの82.7%精度に対し81.6%を72%のthought tokenで達成。token budgetに応じたLLM推論計算削減としてaccept。
